public_rationale: Macnica documented a marked increase in disclosed Japanese web breaches, and JPCERT/CC documented continuing October attack activity, including misuse of AI tools. Together they support the ordinary reading of a growing, ongoing wave. They do not show that every attack involved AI.
limitations: The quantitative series covers selected publicly disclosed web breaches.
The October 23 JPCERT update describes activity before the post but was published afterward.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: There is a growing, ongoing wave of cyberattacks in Japan.

statement.excerpt: There is also a growing, ongoing wave of cyberattacks in Japan.
statement.document_title: Breaking news: U.S. banks are taking hits from AI agents

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that numerous attacks against Japanese organizations were continuing and had increased relative to earlier activity.
The surrounding references to October incidents make October 1–22, 2026 the current observation window. Earlier figures provide the comparison needed to assess growth.
The sentence does not explicitly say every attack involved AI. Its surrounding context suggests AI involvement, which is assessed separately.
criteria.support_condition: Primary incident records or credible security monitoring show an increased cluster of attacks against Japanese organizations continuing into the observation window.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable, sufficiently comprehensive records show that the reported increase did not occur or that the purported wave was no longer ongoing.

evidence.locator: Section 2, 被害傾向, paragraph below Figure 1
evidence.explanation: Macnica reports 119 disclosed breaches through October 6, including 81 disclosed since July, compared with 84 in all of 2025. This supports a growing wave, while measuring disclosures of a selected breach category rather than attack dates or every Japanese cyberattack.

evidence.locator: Section II, Case E, October 23 update
evidence.explanation: JPCERT/CC confirms attacks using AI penetration-testing platforms and lists associated activity dates extending through October 20. Those dates represent observed attacks or estimated operation of attack infrastructure, supporting continuation during the target window and some AI involvement.
